title: KRL MCP
excerpt: A fully self-contained MCP server for Jakarta's KRL Commuter schedules — Go, zero infrastructure, the whole pinned data snapshot embedded in one ~15 MB binary via go:embed.
body:
## Overview

`krl-mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets any MCP host (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor) answer questions about Jakarta's KRL Commuter trains: departure boards, line catalogs, nearest-station lookups, and a direct-trip planner. It is deliberately zero-infrastructure — no database, no cache, no network, no Docker. The open-krl schedule snapshot (~5 MB of artifacts) is pinned in the repo and embedded into the executable at build time, so the entire deployment story is `go install` + `claude mcp add`, running from any working directory.

It is the MCP face of [krl-schedule-service](https://github.com/athallarizky/krl-schedule-service) — my production system with a REST API, Postgres, Redis, and a trip planner. krl-mcp ports the same query logic over the same data contract into plain in-memory scans, proving the domain logic stands on its own.

## Technical Architecture & Flow

```
boards/*.json ──────┐
stations.json ──────┤  parse once  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
GTFS stop_times ────┼─────────────▶│  in-memory store (~5 MB RAM) │
GTFS trips ─────────┘              └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                  │ stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0)
                                                  ▼
                                        MCP host (Claude Code, ...)
```

**The embed.** `asset.go` `go:embed`s the pinned snapshot; the store parses it once at boot into plain slices and maps. One static ~15 MB binary, no working-directory assumptions — an MCP host can spawn it from anywhere.

**SQL becomes memory structures.** What the production service runs as SQL becomes prebuilt indexes here: the planner's trip self-join is a `stop → (trip, seq)` index; line colors are reduced in-memory; the JSON output shapes are byte-compatible with the prod API, and every golden assertion in the test suite was verified against the artifacts before being written.

**Station resolution, 4 tiers.** `"Tanah Tinggi"`, `"tanah tinggi"`, `"TANAHTINGGI"`, and `"THI"` all resolve: exact code → exact name → normalized → substring, implemented as three maps plus a fallback scan.

**The service-day clock.** `24:04` means 00:04 after midnight *of the same service day* — the GTFS convention that keeps late-night trains sortable. The planner accepts hours up to 47.

**The honesty contract.** When no direct trip exists, `plan_trip` returns `meta.transfer_candidates` — the stops where a one-transfer route *is* possible — so an LLM caller can reason about transfers from data instead of inventing routes. Empty means none exists. Likewise `get_trip_stops` exists because a headsign is not a route: train `5133D` says "ANGKE" but runs the southern ring via Manggarai.

## Six Tools

| Tool | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `get_stations` | The 111-station catalog (Jabodetabek + Yogyakarta–Solo) with coordinates |
| `get_departures` | One station's departure board in a time window |
| `get_lines` | The commercial lines with canonical colors |
| `plan_trip` | Direct-trip planner: `depart_at` or `arrive_by`, with intermediate stops |
| `find_nearest_station` | GPS coordinate → closest stations with distances |
| `get_trip_stops` | One train's full ordered stop sequence — the auditable route narrative |

## Engineering Notes

- **Dogfooding as QA:** the LLM itself surfaced three real bugs — a relative data path that silently served empty boards, a name-resolution gap between description and code, and a route hallucination caused by missing intermediate-stop data (fixed by exposing `via` + `get_trip_stops`, the origin of the honesty contract).
- **CI from push one:** the release pipeline builds 5-platform binaries automatically; CI (vet + test) once caught an unanchored `.gitignore` pattern that had silently excluded `cmd/` from the public repo — the local build worked, strangers' clones didn't.
- **Licensing split:** code is MIT; the bundled open-krl data is CC-BY 4.0 (OSM coordinates ODbL) — attribution lives in `NOTICE`, kept explicit and separate.
architecture:
krl-mcp/
├── asset.go              # go:embed — pinned boards/stations/GTFS snapshot in-binary
├── cmd/krl-mcp/main.go   # stdio entry point (JSON-RPC), cwd-independent
├── internal/server/      # MCP layer: 6 tools over go-sdk + e2e test (builds & spawns own binary)
├── internal/store/       # in-memory store: 4-tier station resolution, planner,
│                         #   stop→(trip,seq) index, service-day clock (h ≤ 47)
├── data/                 # pinned open-krl artifacts + manifest (CC-BY 4.0 / ODbL)
├── Makefile · NOTICE · LICENSE (MIT)
└── .github/workflows/    # CI (vet+test) + Release (5-platform binaries)
…
